title: What did you see?
hook: An action and an explanation are different statements.

knows: Animals can act and respond to conditions.
doesNotKnow: A toy drawing shows an animal’s paw moving back and forth on a branch. Which statement records the depicted action?

misconception: One observed behavior always supports a broad or causal conclusion.
objective: A toy drawing shows an animal’s paw moving back and forth on a branch. Which statement records the depicted action?

claims.text: A toy drawing shows an animal’s paw moving back and forth on a branch. Which statement records the depicted action? The two panels show the paw at different positions on the branch, with arrows indicating its back-and-forth motion. The action is depicted; a motive such as wanting attention is an interpretation. This is an illustrative sequence, not a real video or evidence of the animal’s feelings.
claims.source: Source lead, not checked: OpenStax Biology 2e, Behavioral Biology, https://openstax.org/books/biology-2e/pages/45-7-behavioral-biology

claims.text: The panels show a stipulated illustrative scenario, not observations or measurements of real animals.
A bird pecks a door. Which sentence is a direct observation? Pecking is visible; the stated motives are interpretations.
